newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian protesters and police clash, injured.
newsitem.headline: Albanian protesters and police clash, injured.

text.p: Albanian protesters hurled scores of stones at riot police as they tried to force their way to the centre of Tirana on Thursday, eyewitnesses said.
Police moved in with truncheons, hitting protesters and firing volleys of live rounds into the air to disperse the angry crowd of several hundred people.
"Why did you hit us? How much did (President Sali) Berisha pay you? You should defend the people not thieves," screamed one old woman caught up in the fray.
Scores of stones were thrown and witnesses counted at least four people who were bleeding, either from stones or being hit by police.
The clashes took place after some 7,000 anti-government protesters demonstrated peacefully at a soccer field in an outer suburb of the capital.
The witnesses said a group of about 1,000 demonstrators broke off from the main group and started to march toward the city centre.
A police cordon trying to hold them back gave way and the protesters came up against riot police. Rocks were thrown and then riot police began throwing stones at the protesters.
Many demonstrators chanted "Vlore, Vlore. Down with the dictatorship". They were referring to the southern Albanian town where three people died in riots last week.
Albania has been rocked by a month of riots and protests since five fraudulent pyramid investment schemes collapsed in January, wiping out the savings of tens of thousands of people.
Penniless investors have blamed the right-wing government of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi and Berisha, saying they failed to regulate the schemes or to warn investors of their dangers.
Police permitted the demonstration by opposition parties on Thursday but only in the distant suburb while Berisha addressed a peaceful rally of some 5,000 supporters in the centre of the capital.
Witnesses said that the police had again taken control but protesters were regrouping and trying to move towards Tirana's centre.
